database_summary: Relational SQLite schema for a small college scheduling/HR system. Core entities: Buildings, Class_Rooms, Classes, Subjects, Categories, Departments, Staff/Faculty, Students, Majors, and enrollment/status tables. The model mixes descriptive reference/dimension tables (Buildings, Categories, Majors, Student_Class_Status), current-state/person tables (Staff, Students, Faculty), and event/relationship tables that capture associations or occurrences (Classes, Student_Schedules, Faculty_Classes, Faculty_Subjects, Faculty_Categories). Keys and foreign keys are provided but some many-to-many bridge tables are modeled with unusual primary key declarations which may be DDL errors; use the supplied FK relationships as intended. Typical query patterns will join classes -> class_rooms -> buildings, classes -> subjects -> categories, classes -> faculty via Faculty_Classes, and students -> student_schedules -> classes.

accepted.name: classes_with_room_building
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  Classes.ClassID,
  Classes.SubjectID,
  Classes.ClassRoomID,
  Classes.Credits,
  Classes.StartDate,
  Classes.StartTime,
  Classes.Duration,
  Classes.MondaySchedule,
  Classes.TuesdaySchedule,
  Classes.WednesdaySchedule,
  Classes.ThursdaySchedule,
  Classes.FridaySchedule,
  Classes.SaturdaySchedule,
  Class_Rooms.ClassRoomID AS ClassRoomID,
  Class_Rooms.BuildingCode AS BuildingCode,
  Class_Rooms.PhoneAvailable AS PhoneAvailable,
  Buildings.BuildingCode AS BuildingCode_1,
  Buildings.BuildingName AS BuildingName,
  Buildings.NumberOfFloors AS NumberOfFloors,
  Buildings.ElevatorAccess AS ElevatorAccess,
  Buildings.SiteParkingAvailable AS SiteParkingAvailable
FROM Classes
LEFT JOIN Class_Rooms ON Classes.ClassRoomID = Class_Rooms.ClassRoomID
LEFT JOIN Buildings ON Class_Rooms.BuildingCode = Buildings.BuildingCode
accepted.description: One row per class offering enriched with its classroom and building attributes. Useful when queries need class scheduling info together with room and building features (e.g., accessibility, phone availability, building name). | Use for: List classes with their room and building details; Find classes held in buildings with elevator access; Count classes per building or room

accepted.name: classes_with_subject_category
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  Classes.ClassID,
  Classes.SubjectID,
  Classes.ClassRoomID,
  Classes.Credits,
  Classes.StartDate,
  Classes.StartTime,
  Classes.Duration,
  Classes.MondaySchedule,
  Classes.TuesdaySchedule,
  Classes.WednesdaySchedule,
  Classes.ThursdaySchedule,
  Classes.FridaySchedule,
  Classes.SaturdaySchedule,
  Subjects.SubjectID AS SubjectID_1,
  Subjects.CategoryID AS CategoryID,
  Subjects.SubjectCode AS SubjectCode,
  Subjects.SubjectName AS SubjectName,
  Subjects.SubjectPreReq AS SubjectPreReq,
  Subjects.SubjectDescription AS SubjectDescription,
  Categories.CategoryID AS CategoryID_1,
  Categories.CategoryDescription AS CategoryDescription,
  Categories.DepartmentID AS DepartmentID
FROM Classes
LEFT JOIN Subjects ON Classes.SubjectID = Subjects.SubjectID
LEFT JOIN Categories ON Subjects.CategoryID = Categories.CategoryID
accepted.description: One row per class offering joined to its subject and the subject's category. Use this when analyzing classes by academic category or subject attributes. | Use for: Aggregate classes by category or department; Find classes for a given subject or pre-requisite; Join class scheduling with subject descriptions

accepted.name: faculty_with_staff_info
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  Faculty.StaffID,
  Faculty.Title,
  Faculty.Status,
  Faculty.Tenured,
  Staff.StaffID AS StaffID_1,
  Staff.StfFirstName AS StfFirstName,
  Staff.StfLastname AS StfLastname,
  Staff.StfStreetAddress AS StfStreetAddress,
  Staff.StfCity AS StfCity,
  Staff.StfState AS StfState,
  Staff.StfZipCode AS StfZipCode,
  Staff.StfAreaCode AS StfAreaCode,
  Staff.StfPhoneNumber AS StfPhoneNumber,
  Staff.Salary AS Salary,
  Staff.DateHired AS DateHired,
  Staff.Position AS Position
FROM Faculty
LEFT JOIN Staff ON Faculty.StaffID = Staff.StaffID
accepted.description: One row per faculty member combining Faculty specialization attributes with the base Staff contact and employment fields. Useful for personnel reports and joins to department or class assignments. | Use for: List faculty contact info and tenure status; Filter faculty by hire date, salary, or status; Join faculty to classes or subjects for scheduling

accepted.name: student_enrollments_with_status_class
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  Student_Schedules.StudentID,
  Student_Schedules.ClassID,
  Student_Schedules.ClassStatus,
  Student_Schedules.Grade,
  Students.StudentID AS StudentID_1,
  Students.StudFirstName AS StudFirstName,
  Students.StudLastName AS StudLastName,
  Students.StudGPA AS StudGPA,
  Students.StudMajor AS StudMajor,
  Student_Class_Status.ClassStatus AS ClassStatus_1,
  Student_Class_Status.ClassStatusDescription AS ClassStatusDescription,
  Classes.ClassID AS ClassID_1,
  Classes.SubjectID AS SubjectID,
  Classes.StartDate AS StartDate,
  Classes.StartTime AS StartTime
FROM Student_Schedules
LEFT JOIN Students ON Student_Schedules.StudentID = Students.StudentID
LEFT JOIN Student_Class_Status ON Student_Schedules.ClassStatus = Student_Class_Status.ClassStatus
LEFT JOIN Classes ON Student_Schedules.ClassID = Classes.ClassID
accepted.description: One row per student-class enrollment combining Student_Schedules with Students and Student_Class_Status and basic class info. Useful to analyze grades, enrollment statuses, and to connect students to class metadata. | Use for: Compute student grades/GPAs for classes or majors; Count enrollments by status (enrolled/completed); List students in a class with their contact info

accepted.name: faculty_subject_proficiency
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  SubjectID,
  COUNT(StaffID) AS num_instructors,
  AVG(ProficiencyRating) AS avg_proficiency
FROM Faculty_Subjects
GROUP BY SubjectID
accepted.description: Aggregate view at the subject level summarizing faculty proficiency counts and average proficiency for each SubjectID. Use to find subjects with many proficient instructors or high average proficiency. | Use for: Which subjects have the most/least faculty coverage; Average proficiency by subject

accepted.name: class_counts_by_building
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  Class_Rooms.BuildingCode,
  COUNT(Classes.ClassID) AS classes_in_building
FROM Classes
JOIN Class_Rooms ON Classes.ClassRoomID = Class_Rooms.ClassRoomID
GROUP BY Class_Rooms.BuildingCode
accepted.description: Counts of classes scheduled per building (based on the classroom's BuildingCode). Useful for utilization analysis or building-level scheduling reports. | Use for: Compare class counts across buildings; Identify under/over-utilized buildings

accepted.name: faculty_teaching_load
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  Faculty_Classes.StaffID,
  COUNT(Faculty_Classes.ClassID) AS classes_taught,
  COUNT(DISTINCT Classes.SubjectID) AS distinct_subjects_taught
FROM Faculty_Classes
LEFT JOIN Classes ON Faculty_Classes.ClassID = Classes.ClassID
GROUP BY Faculty_Classes.StaffID
accepted.description: One row per faculty member with counts of classes they teach and distinct subjects taught. Useful for workload or assignment balancing. | Use for: Find faculty with the heaviest teaching load; Balance assignments by subject coverage

accepted.name: students_with_major
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  Students.StudentID,
  Students.StudFirstName,
  Students.StudLastName,
  Students.StudGPA,
  Students.StudMajor,
  Majors.MajorID AS MajorID,
  Majors.Major AS Major
FROM Students
LEFT JOIN Majors ON Students.StudMajor = Majors.MajorID
accepted.description: One row per student augmented with their major name from Majors. Useful for cohort selection, aggregation by major, or linking student demographics to academic program. | Use for: Aggregate student GPA by major; List students in a particular major

accepted.name: faculty_categories_bridge
accepted.description: Exploded bridge rows listing faculty-to-category assignments. One row per StaffID and CategoryID pairing; useful for pivoting faculty by category or filtering faculty by category membership. | Use for: Find all faculty in a given category; Pivot faculty counts by category

accepted.name: class_schedule_weekdays_flag
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  ClassID,
  MondaySchedule,
  TuesdaySchedule,
  WednesdaySchedule,
  ThursdaySchedule,
  FridaySchedule,
  SaturdaySchedule,
  (COALESCE(MondaySchedule,0) + COALESCE(TuesdaySchedule,0) + COALESCE(WednesdaySchedule,0) + COALESCE(ThursdaySchedule,0) + COALESCE(FridaySchedule,0) + COALESCE(SaturdaySchedule,0)) AS meeting_days_count,
  (CASE WHEN (COALESCE(MondaySchedule,0) + COALESCE(TuesdaySchedule,0) + COALESCE(WednesdaySchedule,0) + COALESCE(ThursdaySchedule,0) + COALESCE(FridaySchedule,0)) > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS meets_weekday_flag
FROM Classes
accepted.description: Normalized per-class boolean flags indicating whether the class meets on any weekday (Mon-Fri) and total meeting_days count. Useful for filtering classes that meet during the standard week or weighting by meeting frequency. | Use for: Filter classes that meet on weekdays vs weekends; Weight scheduling by number of meeting days

accepted.name: latest_hired_staff
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  StaffID,
  StfFirstName,
  StfLastname,
  DateHired,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY DateHired DESC) AS hire_date_rank
FROM Staff
accepted.description: Per-staff ranking by DateHired to enable latest/new hires selection. One row per Staff with hire_date_rank; useful to pick newest or compare seniority. Does not filter to top-N; preserves ranks for downstream selection. | Use for: Select the most recently hired staff members; Analyze tenure or seniority cohorts
